gen: Creates new content from learned patterns; generated content still needs appropriate review.
classification: Assigns inputs to predefined categories rather than generating open-ended content.
regression: Predicts a numeric quantity rather than producing new prose, images, or video.
rules: Applies explicit rules and is suitable when an exact prescribed result is required without probabilistic generation.
ml: Learns useful patterns from data instead of requiring every decision rule to be manually programmed.
deep: Is a subset of machine learning using neural networks with multiple layers to learn representations.
ai: Is the broad field of systems performing tasks associated with human intelligence; it includes more than generative models.
supervised: Learns from examples paired with known target labels or outcomes.
unsupervised: Finds patterns or groupings without supplied target labels.
reinforcement: Learns actions through interaction and reward or penalty feedback.
structured: Uses a predefined organization such as rows and typed columns in a relational table.
unstructured: Includes free-form content such as prose, audio, and images without a fixed tabular schema.
labeled: Pairs examples with assigned tags, categories, or target outcomes; a structured file is not automatically labeled.
unlabeled: Lacks supplied target annotations; it may still contain useful patterns and can be structured or unstructured.
quality: Improve data accuracy, completeness, consistency, and relevance
Addresses defects in the source evidence; greater model capacity does not automatically repair incorrect data.
access: Ensure authorized data is available in a usable format
Makes relevant evidence practically usable while retaining permissions and governance; accessibility does not mean public access.
ingest: Collects or brings source information into the data workflow before later processing.
prepare: Cleans, transforms, and organizes collected data for its intended use.
train: Learns model parameters from data; it is different from serving a trained model to users.
deploy: Makes a trained or selected model available for application use.
manage: Monitors, versions, maintains, and improves models after deployment as conditions change.
inference: Uses a trained model to produce an output for new input without inherently updating its weights.
fm: Is broadly pretrained and can support or be adapted to multiple downstream tasks.
llm: Is designed to process and generate language using learned patterns; fluency is not proof of truth.
multi: Can work with multiple input or output modalities, subject to the selected model capabilities.
diffusion: Learns to reverse a noise process and is commonly used for image generation.
choose: Evaluate model fit against business and operational requirements
Considers modality, quality, context, security, availability, customization, latency, and total cost.
largest: Choose only the largest available model
Can increase cost or latency without establishing task suitability or meeting governance requirements.
cheapest: Choose only the lowest token price
Ignores quality, retries, review effort, latency, and other costs of the full solution.
infra: Provides compute, accelerators, storage, networking, and supporting resources used to train and serve AI systems.
platform: Provides APIs and services for developing, deploying, and managing models and AI applications.
agent: Combines a model or decision logic with tools and a goal-oriented workflow to observe and act.
application: Provides the user-facing experience that embeds AI capabilities into a business workflow.
gemini: Supports broad multimodal and language tasks, with specific modalities and limits depending on the chosen model.
gemma: Offers open-weight model options for compatible customized or local deployments, subject to license and hardware requirements.
imagen: Focuses on generating and editing images from supported inputs, rather than serving as a video-generation family.
veo: Focuses on video generation from supported prompts or image inputs, subject to model availability and capabilities.
draft: Use generative AI to draft content with suitable review
Fits open-ended content creation when quality, rights, and risk controls are addressed.
biggerdata: Add more data without checking its quality
Can amplify errors or irrelevant content and is not a substitute for data validation.
prompt: Refines instructions, examples, and context at inference time without changing learned model weights.
tpu: Are Google-designed accelerators optimized for supported machine-learning workloads; suitability still depends on the workload.
gpu: Provide parallel acceleration widely used for compatible training and inference workloads.
cpu: Handle general computation but do not denote a specialized parallel AI accelerator family.
managed: Use managed cloud capacity with workload-aware scaling
Can reduce infrastructure operating burden while capacity, quotas, reliability, and cost still require planning.
open: Evaluate model and framework choice through an open ecosystem
Supports flexibility across eligible first-party, third-party, and open models rather than assuming one model suits every use case.
controls: Assess enterprise security, privacy, governance, and service controls
Checks the actual service, account, configuration, and terms instead of assuming all AI products handle data identically.
lowcode: Use supported prebuilt APIs and low-code or no-code tools
Can lower development barriers for suitable tasks without eliminating testing, governance, or all technical work.
gems: Provide reusable personalized assistant instructions for supported tasks; they are not automatically a fully deployed enterprise agent platform.
geminiapp: Provides a conversational user-facing assistant experience; its features and data terms depend on account and offering.
workspace: Brings supported AI assistance into Workspace applications such as Gmail and Docs, subject to edition and availability.
enterprise: Supports enterprise information discovery and custom agent experiences across authorized organizational sources, subject to configuration.
notebook: Help users work with selected source materials through summaries and source-oriented questions, subject to the available offering.
search: Agent Search on Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform
Provides managed enterprise search and retrieval capabilities for supported business content and applications.
googlesearch: Google Search and supported Search grounding
Provides access to public world information; it does not automatically grant access to confidential enterprise repositories.
conversational: Supports customer-facing conversational experiences and task interactions, subject to configured capabilities and integrations.
assist: Provides supported guidance and assistance to human contact-center agents during their work.
insights: Analyzes customer conversations to identify themes, patterns, and operational improvement opportunities.
ccaas: Google Cloud Contact Center as a Service
Provides cloud-based contact-center capabilities rather than merely analyzing historical conversation text.
garden: Helps teams discover and evaluate supported Google, third-party, and open models, subject to model-specific terms and availability.
automl: Supports training suitable models with reduced manual model-development effort; it is not a general guarantee that every task can be automated.
customagents: Use Agent Platform to build a controlled custom agent
Combines model capabilities, approved tools, knowledge, and orchestration for a purpose-specific business workflow.
ragapi: Use supported RAG APIs for a custom retrieval workflow
Provides building blocks for retrieving and supplying external evidence when a team needs application-specific integration.
agentstudio: Is positioned in the retrieved guide for building production-oriented AI applications with cloud platform capabilities.
aistudio: Supports rapid prototyping and experimentation with supported Gemini capabilities; a prototype alone does not establish production readiness.
storage: Provides object storage for files and datasets rather than a complete conversation agent or a transactional relational database.
run: Provides managed hosting for compatible containerized applications and services, subject to runtime and service configuration.
functions: Supports suitable event-driven functions and tool implementations; naming varies across guide and service generations.
stt: Converts supported speech audio into text rather than synthesizing spoken output.
tts: Converts text into supported synthesized speech rather than transcribing input audio.
translation: Translates supported text between languages; it does not by itself constitute structured document extraction.
doctranslation: Translates supported formatted documents while aiming to preserve document layout, subject to format limitations.
docai: Extracts and processes information from supported documents, including structured fields for suitable processors.
vision: Analyzes supported image content, such as objects, text, and landmarks; it is distinct from generating a new image.
video: Analyzes supported video content and extracts useful annotations rather than generating new video.
nlp: Analyzes existing text for supported tasks such as sentiment, entities, and classification.
database: Use an authorized database lookup tool
Retrieves authoritative structured business records through enforced access rather than inventing live facts from model weights.
tool: Use a validated function or extension to an external service
Lets trusted application code perform an authorized real-world operation; generated text claiming success is not proof of execution.
hallucination: Is generated content that appears plausible but is factually wrong or unsupported by the available evidence.
cutoff: Limits what facts could be learned during training; the model does not inherently know later events without additional evidence or tools.
rag: Retrieves external evidence, adds it to the request context, and generates an answer without inherently updating model weights.
tune: Updates model parameters using suitable task-specific training data; it is not automatically the best way to supply frequently changing facts.
human: Uses qualified people to verify, approve, correct, or escalate outputs, especially where consequences are significant.
zero: Gives task instructions without a worked example in the prompt.
one: Provides one worked demonstration of the desired task behavior in the prompt.
few: Provides several worked demonstrations of the desired input-output behavior in the prompt.
role: Specifies a perspective or function to guide response tone and focus; it does not grant expertise or authority.
chaining: Uses linked prompt steps or exchanges so one stage informs later stages of a larger task.
cot: Uses intermediate-step demonstrations or structured problem-solving guidance; it is not a guarantee of correctness or access to private internal reasoning.
react: Combines deciding a next step with permitted external actions and observations in a controlled loop.
firstparty: Ground with authorized first-party enterprise data
Uses approved organizational evidence for private business facts, with appropriate access controls.
thirdparty: Ground with a licensed or approved third-party source
Uses permitted information from an external provider when that source is authoritative for the requirement.
world: Ground with relevant public world information
Uses appropriate public evidence, such as supported Search grounding, rather than assuming private records are publicly available.
temperature: Adjust temperature to control sampling variability
Lower values generally make sampling more focused and higher values more varied; neither guarantees factual correctness.
topp: Restricts the candidate token set using cumulative probability mass rather than a fixed response length.
length: Set an appropriate maximum output length
Caps generated output tokens within supported limits; too low a cap can truncate an answer.
context: Bounds the information a model can consider within a request according to model-specific limits.
token: Is a model-dependent input or output unit that may represent a word fragment; token count is not always word count.
monitor: Continuously evaluate, version, and monitor the solution
Tracks quality, usage, regressions, security updates, and changing conditions instead of assuming launch completes maintenance.
softprompt: Learns task-specific prompt representations while keeping base model weights frozen in supported approaches; it differs from manually rewriting prompt text.
safety: Configure and test appropriate safety controls
Can reduce supported harmful content but does not guarantee factual accuracy, authorization, or complete risk elimination.
priority: Prioritize measurable business value with feasible data and manageable risk
Selects use cases using value, readiness, constraints, and consequences rather than novelty alone.
pilot: Start with a bounded pilot and defined success criteria
Tests value and risk on a controlled scope before broad expansion.
roi: Evaluate total benefits against total implementation and operating costs
Accounts for integration, model use, review, training, and maintenance rather than relying only on the price of a token.
kpi: Define outcome-focused baseline and success metrics
Measures the business goal, such as verified resolution or handling time, alongside quality and safety measures.
adoption: Plan training, workflow change, feedback, and ongoing support
Addresses the people and process changes required for useful adoption rather than treating deployment as automatic acceptance.
stakeholders: Align business, technical, security, and affected-user stakeholders
Connects goals, feasibility, controls, and user needs before decisions become difficult to reverse.
saif: Provides a framework for securing AI systems and addressing AI-specific risks across their lifecycle; it is not a guarantee or an automatic certification.
iam: Controls which principals may perform supported actions on resources through roles and policies.
scc: Helps identify and manage supported security findings and posture information; it is not a source-document quality evaluator.
securelife: Apply security controls throughout the AI lifecycle
Addresses source data, development, deployment, access, monitoring, and updates rather than only the launch endpoint.
transparent: Disclose AI use, relevant limits, and review pathways
Helps stakeholders understand the role of the system and limitations rather than treating generated answers as unquestionable authority.
privacy: Minimize and protect personal data for the approved purpose
Limits unnecessary collection, use, retention, and disclosure according to applicable obligations.
pseudonym: Replaces direct identifiers with aliases while a linkage or re-identification route may remain; it is not the same as irreversible anonymity.
anonym: Aims to prevent identification under the relevant standard; simply removing names does not automatically achieve it.
fair: Evaluate relevant subgroups and address inappropriate disparities
Checks uneven outcomes and representation with appropriate data and review; overall accuracy can conceal harmful differences.
accountable: Assign decision ownership, explanations, and escalation responsibilities
Makes people or teams answerable for AI impacts and supports review of consequential outcomes.
